subject: SIG: Request for encryption controls + KMS/HSM rotation evidence
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmehealth.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up - encryption specifics and evidence request

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for agreeing to help with our SIG review. The security team at Acme HealthTech is validating encryption controls across vendors and we need a few specific items clarified and any supporting artifacts you can share: 

- TLS in transit: minimum supported TLS versions and cipher suites used for public endpoints (API, console).
- Encryption at rest: algorithms used for persistent model/artifact storage and s3 buckets.
- KMS/HSM: provider(s) used for key management, whether CMKs are customer-specific, and HSM vendor (if applicable).
- Key rotation: automated rotation frequency for CMKs and DEKs, and process for emergency rekey/compromise.
- Evidence: rotation logs for the last 12 months, a config dump or diagram showing envelope encryption, and a short artifact proving HSM usage (if you use CloudHSM or equivalent).

Can you point me to the artifacts (pdfs/csvs) or paste the short answers? We’re targeting completion of this section by Friday.

Appreciate it,
Marta
Security Programs
Acme HealthTech

Attachment: SIG_Questions_v2.xlsx (referenced)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up - encryption specifics and evidence request

Marta — thanks for the list. Looping in Soojin (Security) and Laura (Compliance) to provide the details and artifacts. We should be able to get the rotation logs and a short HSM proof over the next 48 hours. Preliminary answers below; Soojin will follow with the artifacts.

Quick answers:
- TLS in transit: TLS 1.2+ supported; TLS 1.3 preferred on public endpoints. We maintain a documented cipher suite baseline and disable known-weak ciphers.
- At rest: AES-256-GCM for data at rest, envelope encryption using a customer root CMK where applicable.
- KMS/HSM: Primary KMS is AWS KMS (CMKs). For customers on Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and customer HSM attachments (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM).
- Rotation: DEKs are rotated automatically per workload (configurable); CMKs follow a 12-mo rotation recommendation for keys we manage. Emergency rekey procedure exists — will share runbook.

Sooj, Laura — can you attach: rotation logs CSV, a short HSM proof text, and the config dump for envelope encryption? Thanks.

—Aditya
Head of Solutions (on behalf of Security Coord.)
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmehealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up - encryption specifics and evidence request

Hi all — providing the detailed answers and attaching the requested artifacts (see attachments list below). I’ll summarize key points here and call out what we’ve attached.

1) TLS / In-transit
- Public endpoints (API & Console): support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. We prioritize TLS 1.3; TLS 1.2 remains for older client compatibility.
- Cipher suites: we enforce a modern baseline (AEAD ciphers only, ECDHE key exchange). Weak ciphers (RC4, 3DES) are disabled.
- Evidence: tls_cipher_snapshot.txt contains an authoritative snapshot from our edge proxy (timestamped).

2) Encryption at rest
- Data at rest for model artifacts and customer data: AES-256-GCM with per-object DEKs. DEKs are wrapped with a CMK (envelope encryption).
- Storage: object storage is backed by cloud provider (S3-compatible) with server-side encryption enforced; where customers require customer-managed keys we configure SSE-CMS or bucket-level encryption with the customer CMK.
- Evidence: sig_kms_config.yaml (sanitized) shows our envelope encryption config and CMK binding patterns.

3) KMS / HSM details
- Default: AWS KMS with AWS-managed HSM-backed CMKs. For Dedicated/Private customers we support customer KMS (BYOK) and CloudHSM clusters or on-prem HSM attachments.
- CMKs: we create per-tenant CMK aliases for isolation on Dedicated/Private plans; hosted customers share service CMKs but DEK separation is maintained by per-tenant DEKs.
- HSM proof: cloudhsm_proof.txt is a short export showing an HSM-backed key metadata (no raw key material) and the KMS key origin field.

4) Rotation policy & emergency rekey
- DEKs (data encryption keys): rotated automatically by the service per configured TTL; common default is 90 days but configurable per workload.
- CMKs (key encryption keys): for keys we manage we recommend and can enforce rotation every 12 months. For customer-owned CMKs, rotation is driven by customer policy; we provide rotation tooling and a documented process.
- Emergency rekey: documented runbook (internal) — immediate rewrap of active DEKs, rolling re-encryption where necessary, and incident report. We’ll provide redacted runbook excerpt if needed.
- Evidence: kms_rotation_audit.csv contains rotation event timestamps and KMS key version ids for the past 12 months (redacted to remove customer PII).

5) Key material provenance and backups
- Root key material is HSM-generated within the KMS/HSM provider; we do not store raw key material in plaintext outside of the provider.
- Backups: customer CMKs may be exported only via provider tooling where supported (example: CloudHSM backed key archival). We maintain offline-wrapped backups for disaster recovery; proof of backup rotations can be provided on request.

Attachments included (sanitized):
- sig_kms_config.yaml (sanitized config dump showing envelope encryption bindings)
- kms_rotation_audit.csv (rotation audit, redacted)
- cloudhsm_proof.txt (HSM-backed key metadata, no secrets)
- tls_cipher_snapshot.txt (edge proxy cipher snapshot)

If Acme needs a signed attestation or a redacted runbook excerpt for the emergency rekey flow, indicate and we’ll coordinate with Legal to provide.

—Soojin
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up - encryption specifics and evidence request

Hi Marta — thanks for the patience. Attaching the artifacts Soojin prepared; below is a concise answers summary you can drop into the SIG spreadsheet: 

- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (prefer 1.3), AEAD/ECDHE cipher suites only, weak ciphers disabled. (See tls_cipher_snapshot.txt)
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM with envelope encryption (DEKs wrapped by CMKs). (See sig_kms_config.yaml)
- KMS/HSM: AWS KMS by default; CloudHSM / on-prem HSM available for Private customers. CMK isolation on Dedicated/Private, service CMKs for hosted with per-tenant DEKs. (See cloudhsm_proof.txt)
- Rotation: DEKs default 90-day rotation (configurable); CMKs recommended 12-mo rotation; emergency rekey runbook available on request. (See kms_rotation_audit.csv)

Attachments included: sig_kms_config.yaml, kms_rotation_audit.csv, cloudhsm_proof.txt, tls_cipher_snapshot.txt.

If you want a redacted copy of the emergency rekey runbook or an attestation signed by our security leadership, let me know and we’ll route that through Legal. Can we set a quick 20-min sync tomorrow to close this section? I’m available 10:00–12:00 PDT.

Best,
Aditya Rao

1) Can you provide the redacted emergency rekey runbook excerpt (steps + owner + escalation contacts) — redacted for internal emails/PII is fine.
2) For our audit evidence we need a signed confirmation that the kms_rotation_audit.csv reflects all rotation events for your managed CMKs over the past 12 months. Either a short signed email from your security leadership or a DocuSign link for a one-page attestation will work.

If you can drop those by EOD Thursday we should be able to close this out. Appreciate the clarity — will loop Procurement if we need anything additional.

Cheers,
